mainTopic: Consecrating limbs and fetuses: rereading the משנה, and setting the exact limits of the argument between בר פדא and רבי יוחנן about holiness on fetuses
overview: The amud opens by rereading the משנה about limbs and fetuses. In the new reading, only limbs are consecrated directly, and no תמורה can be made for fetuses while they are in the womb. The גמרא defends this reading by saying the משנה follows רבי יהודה and is talking about a limb the animal cannot live without (a טרפה limb). Next, it tests whether the argument between בר פדא and רבי יוחנן about consecrating fetuses was already argued by תנאים, using two ברייתות about a live fetus found in a slaughtered חטאת. It rejects that link in two ways: the ברייתות argue about when offspring become holy, or one תנא is ruling on two different cases. Then רבי אליעזר's list of flawed animals, and רבי מאיר's comments on it in two versions, seem to show that a fetus can be holy, against בר פדא. Both times the answer is that everyone agrees a healthy fetus in a healthy mother is holy. בר פדא and רבי יוחנן argue only about a fetus inside a blemished mother: does it follow its mother, or is it a separate animal? The amud ends by turning to רבי יוסי's view in the משנה, that swapping using limbs should work for תמורה.

steps.title: A new way to read the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The משנה is reread: limbs can be consecrated and the holiness spreads to the whole animal, so a תמורה can be made for that animal. A limb alone cannot be used to make a תמורה. Fetuses consecrated through their mother cannot have a תמורה made for them.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what the משנה means: one may consecrate limbs, and one may then make a substitute for those animals. But one may not use limbs alone to make a substitute. And fetuses that became holy inside their mother cannot have a substitute made for them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא re-explains the words of the משנה so that it no longer says that fetuses can be consecrated on their own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On a simple reading, 'consecrate' applied to both fetuses and limbs. Now 'consecrate' applies only to limbs, because their holiness spreads to the whole animal. Fetuses appear only in the rule that no תמורה can be made for them while they are inside the mother, and they became holy through the mother.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means (a rereading of a text)
We consecrate (make something holy)
We make a תמורה (swap an ordinary animal for a holy one)
Fetuses, unborn animals
Inside their mother's womb

steps.confusionAlert: The phrase 'ממירין בהן' appears twice with different meanings. First it means making a תמורה for the animal whose limb was consecrated. Then 'לא ממירין בהן' means you cannot use a limb by itself to make a תמורה.

phrases.english: This is what it is saying:
One consecrates limbs, and one makes a substitute for them,
phrases.notes: Once one limb is holy, the whole animal becomes holy, so you can swap another animal for it.

phrases.english: but one does not substitute with them,
and fetuses that became holy in their mother's womb
one does not make a substitute for them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the earlier difficulty (from before this section) that the משנה seemed to say fetuses can be consecrated.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה says fetuses and limbs can both be consecrated directly.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only limbs are consecrated directly. Fetuses are holy through their mother, and no תמורה can be made for them while they are inside her.

steps.title: Can offspring make a תמורה after birth?
steps.stepSummary: The new reading suggests that once the offspring are born, a תמורה can be made for them. But a later משנה says offspring never make a תמורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the משנה is about the offspring of holy animals, then only while they are inside the mother can no תמורה be made. That implies that outside, a תמורה can be made. But we learned in a משנה: the offspring do not make a תמורה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the new reading by drawing an inference from it. That inference contradicts another משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'in their mother's womb' suggest that the rule depends on being unborn. If so, a born offspring could make a תמורה. Yet a later משנה clearly says that offspring of holy animals never make a תמורה.

keyTerms.meaning: Offspring of holy (sacrificial) animals
Outside (after birth)
A substitute: an ordinary animal swapped for a holy one becomes holy too
This implies (introducing an inference)

phrases.english: Regarding offspring of holy animals: in their mother's womb
is when they do not make a substitute,
which implies that outside, they do make one.
But didn't we learn:
The offspring do not make a substitute!

steps.kashyaTarget: The rereading of the משנה in step 1
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The phrase 'in their mother's womb' implies that born offspring can make a תמורה. That contradicts the later משנה saying offspring never make one.

steps.title: The משנה follows רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The answer is that this משנה follows רבי יהודה, who holds that offspring can make a תמורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is this? It is רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by saying that this משנה follows a different תנא, רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The later משנה (offspring do not make a תמורה) is one view. רבי יהודה disagrees and holds that offspring do make a תמורה. So the inference from step 2 is correct according to רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose view is this? (assigning a source to a specific sage)

phrases.english: Whose is this? It is רבי יהודה.
phrases.notes: He means that רבי יהודה holds that offspring can make a substitute, so the two משניות simply follow different sages.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the משנה to a specific תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both משניות follow the same view, so they contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: This משנה follows רבי יהודה, who allows a תמורה for offspring.

steps.title: רבי יהודה does not let a limb's holiness spread
steps.stepSummary: If the משנה follows רבי יהודה, how can consecrating limbs make the whole animal holy? רבי יהודה rejects the rule that saying 'its leg is an עולה' makes the whole animal an עולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it is רבי יהודה, are limbs really consecrated this way? But רבי יהודה does not accept that one who says 'the leg of this animal is an עולה' makes the whole animal an עולה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer of step 3. Assigning the משנה to רבי יהודה clashes with how the משנה was read in step 1.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reading in step 1 assumed that holiness on a limb spreads to the whole animal, so a תמורה can be made for it. But רבי יהודה rejects that spreading. So the משנה cannot be both רבי יהודה and the step 1 reading.

keyTerms.meaning: Limbs, body parts of an animal
He does not hold (that view)
A burnt offering, fully burned on the altar

phrases.english: If it is רבי יהודה,
are limbs consecrated?
phrases.notes: He means: does holiness placed on a limb spread to the whole animal?

phrases.english: But רבי יהודה does not hold
that one who says, 'The leg of this one is a burnt offering' —
the whole animal is a burnt offering!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה, אֵבָרִין מִי קָדְשִׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 3 by pointing to another view of רבי יהודה.
steps.kashyaTarget: Assigning the משנה to רבי יהודה (step 3) together with the reading of step 1
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Step 1 needs holiness to spread from a limb to the whole animal, and רבי יהודה rejects that.

steps.title: A limb the animal cannot live without
steps.stepSummary: The משנה is talking about a limb whose loss would make the animal a טרפה. In that case even רבי יהודה agrees that the holiness spreads to the whole animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: What case are we dealing with here? A limb that would make the animal a טרפה (if it were missing).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by narrowing the case. The משנה is about a vital limb.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה rejects spreading only for a limb the animal can live without. If losing the limb would make the animal a טרפה, the limb is so central that its holiness covers the whole animal. So the משנה can follow רבי יהודה, and the reading from step 1 stands.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here? (limiting a source to a specific case)
An animal with a fatal defect that will not survive

steps.whatToRemember: The rereading holds. The משנה follows רבי יהודה and is talking about a vital limb. It does not prove that a fetus can be consecrated on its own.
steps.whyThisMatters: This protects the view that fetuses cannot be consecrated on their own, even though the משנה seemed at first to say they can.

phrases.english: He said to him:
With what are we dealing here?
With a limb that makes it a טרפה.
phrases.notes: He means a limb that, if it were removed, would leave the animal unable to survive.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 4 by limiting the case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהודה never lets a limb's holiness spread to the whole animal.
steps.terutzMaskana: For a limb whose loss would make the animal a טרפה, even רבי יהודה agrees that the whole animal becomes holy.

steps.title: Proposing a parallel dispute: the first ברייתא about a fetus in a חטאת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the argument about holiness on fetuses matches an argument of תנאים. It begins with a ברייתא that treats a live fetus found in a slaughtered חטאת as a full חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say this is like an argument of תנאים? If someone slaughtered a חטאת and found a live four-month fetus inside it, one ברייתא teaches: it is eaten only by male כהנים, only inside the curtains, and only for one day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a comparison. It brings the first of two ברייתות that it will soon place side by side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ברייתא gives the fetus every eating rule of a חטאת: male כהנים only, inside the Temple courtyard only, and one day only. That only makes sense if the holiness of the mother took hold of the fetus too.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say it is like an argument between תנאים? This is a suggestion that an argument of later scholars was already argued earlier.
A sin offering. Its meat is eaten only by male כהנים, inside the courtyard, for one day and night.
The males of the priesthood
Inside the hangings, meaning within the Temple courtyard

phrases.english: Shall we say it is like an argument of תנאים?
phrases.notes: He means the earlier argument between בר פדא and רבי יוחנן about whether fetuses can become holy.

phrases.english: One who slaughtered a sin offering
and found inside it a live four-month-old fetus,
one ברייתא teaches:
it is eaten only by the males of the priesthood,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵינָהּ נֶאֱכֶלֶת אֶלָּא לִפְנִים מִן הַקְּלָעִים,
phrases.english: and it is eaten only inside the hangings,
and it is eaten only for one day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic. It returns to the question of holiness on fetuses and looks for a source among the תנאים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to this ברייתא, a live fetus found inside a slaughtered חטאת has every eating rule of a חטאת.

steps.title: The opposite ברייתא, and the suggestion that this is an argument of תנאים
steps.stepSummary: A second ברייתא treats the same fetus as ordinary food. The גמרא suggests the two ברייתות argue over whether holiness takes hold of fetuses.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another ברייתא teaches: it may be eaten by anyone, anywhere, but not in the עזרה. Isn't this an argument of תנאים? One holds holiness takes hold of fetuses, and the other holds it does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second ברייתא that rules the opposite way. It then suggests that the two ברייתות are really arguing about whether holiness takes hold of fetuses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The second ברייתא lets anyone eat the fetus anywhere, so it treats the fetus as not holy. Put the two side by side and they look like two opinions: the first says the holiness reached the fetus, the second says it did not. That would mean our later argument was already argued by תנאים.

keyTerms.meaning: The Temple courtyard
Isn't it so that...? The גמרא uses this to offer a likely reading.
Holiness takes hold of fetuses

steps.confusionAlert: The rule that it may not be eaten in the עזרה does not mean the fetus is holy. It means the opposite: it is ordinary food, and ordinary food is not brought into the Temple courtyard to be eaten.

phrases.english: And another ברייתא teaches:
it is eaten by any person,
and such animals may be eaten anywhere,
but they may not be eaten in the Temple courtyard.
Isn't it an argument of תנאים?

phrases.aramaic: דְּמָר סָבַר: קְדוּשָּׁה חָלָה עַל עוּבָּרִין,
phrases.english: One Sage holds: holiness takes hold of fetuses,
phrases.notes: This is the first ברייתא, the one that treats the fetus as a חטאת.

phrases.aramaic: וּמַר סָבַר: אֵין קְדוּשָּׁה חָלָה עַל עוּבָּרִין.
phrases.english: and one Sage holds: holiness does not take hold of fetuses.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the comparison started in step 6 by bringing the opposite ברייתא and drawing a conclusion from the pair.
steps.raayaObject: That the argument over whether holiness takes hold of fetuses is already an argument between תנאים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: Two ברייתות that disagree about how to eat a live fetus found inside a slaughtered חטאת.

steps.title: No: they argue about when offspring become holy
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the suggestion. Both תנאים may agree that holiness can reach a fetus. They argue only over whether the offspring of קדשים become holy at birth or already in the womb.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. These תנאים argue about this: one holds the offspring of קדשים become holy only when they are born, and the other holds they are holy already in their mother's womb.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back. It says the two ברייתות are arguing about something else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is now an animal that was consecrated first and became pregnant afterward. One view says its offspring become holy only at birth. This fetus was never born, so it is ordinary food (second ברייתא). The other view says the offspring are holy already in the womb, so it is a חטאת (first ברייתא).

keyTerms.meaning: They disagree
The offspring of consecrated animals
When they come into being, meaning at birth
In their mother's womb

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up this argument with the one in step 7. The question here is not whether a fetus can ever become holy. It is about when the offspring of a holy animal become holy.

phrases.aramaic: לָא, הָנֵי תַּנָּאֵי בְּהָא קָא מִיפַּלְגִי,
phrases.english: No, these תנאים disagree about this:
one Sage holds:
phrases.notes: This is the second ברייתא, the one that lets anyone eat the fetus.

phrases.english: the offspring of consecrated animals become holy when they come into being,
and one Sage holds:

phrases.aramaic: וַלְדֵי קָדָשִׁים בִּמְעֵי אִמָּן הֵן קְדוֹשִׁים.
phrases.english: the offspring of consecrated animals are holy in their mother's womb.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, הָנֵי תַּנָּאֵי בְּהָא קָא מִיפַּלְגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the link made in step 7 by moving the argument to a different question.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the claim that the ברייתות argue about holiness on fetuses. It still agrees that two תנאים are arguing.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתות can be read as both agreeing that fetuses can become holy. Their argument is about the timing of holiness for offspring that were conceived after the mother was consecrated.

steps.title: Or: one תנא speaking about two different cases
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא offers a second way out. There is no argument at all. One ברייתא speaks of an animal consecrated before it became pregnant, and the other of an animal consecrated while already pregnant.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or you can say it is one תנא. One of these ברייתות speaks of someone who consecrated an animal that became pregnant afterward. The other speaks of someone who consecrated it while it was already pregnant.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second answer. It says both ברייתות come from one תנא who rules differently in two different cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the animal became pregnant after it was consecrated, the fetus did not exist when the animal was made holy, so it is ordinary food. If the animal was already pregnant, the fetus was included in the holiness, so it is a חטאת. This fits the view that holiness does take hold of fetuses, with no argument needed.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you want, say instead. This introduces a second answer.
One תנא, meaning there is no argument at all
She became pregnant
Already pregnant

steps.whatToRemember: There are two ways to explain the two ברייתות about a fetus in a חטאת. (1) They argue over whether offspring become holy in the womb or only at birth. (2) One תנא rules differently depending on whether the animal was consecrated before or after it became pregnant. Either way, the ברייתות do not have to be an argument about whether holiness takes hold of fetuses.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
it is one תנא,
one of these ברייתות —
phrases.notes: This is the second ברייתא, where anyone may eat the fetus.

phrases.english: is about one who consecrates an animal and it became pregnant afterward,
and one of them —
is where he consecrated it while pregnant.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, different rejection of the suggestion in step 7, offered alongside the answer in step 8.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the whole idea that the two ברייתות disagree.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתות are speaking about two different cases, so they do not contradict each other.

steps.title: Flawed animals do not take part in substitution
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר lists five kinds of flawed animals that are 'not holy and do not make holy'. שמואל explains that this means they have no part in תמורה, in either direction.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא says: רבי אליעזר says that a mixed-breed animal, a טרפה, an animal born through its mother's side, a טומטום and an אנדרוגינוס are not holy and do not make holy. שמואל explains: they cannot become holy as a substitute, and they cannot make another animal holy as their substitute.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is bringing a new ברייתא as background. It is setting up the next move, where רבי מאיר's comment on this list will be used to challenge בר פדא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, if you swap a regular animal for a holy one (תמורה), the regular animal becomes holy too. רבי אליעזר says these five flawed animals are left out of that rule. They can't be the animal that becomes holy through the swap, and they can't be the holy animal that passes holiness on to a swapped one.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal born from two different species mixed together
An animal with a fatal injury or defect
An animal born through the side of its mother, not in the normal way
An animal whose sex organs are covered, so we can't tell if it is male or female
An animal with both male and female organs
Swapping a regular animal for a holy one; the regular animal also becomes holy

phrases.english: It is taught: Rabbi Eliezer says:
A mixed-breed animal, and a tereifa,
and one born through the side, a tumtum, and an androginos
are not holy and do not make holy.
And Shmuel said:
They do not become holy as a substitute,
and they do not make another animal holy as a substitute.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new source, which will be used against בר פדא's view on consecrating a fetus.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The five flawed animals cannot become holy through תמורה, and they cannot make another animal holy through תמורה.

steps.title: רבי מאיר's comment shows a fetus can become holy
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר asks how animals that can't become holy could ever 'make holy'. He answers that this only happens if they became holy before the flaw, for example a consecrated fetus later born through the side. The גמרא infers that a fetus can be consecrated, which challenges בר פדא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר said: since these animals can't become holy, how could they make another animal holy? This only happens when someone consecrated an animal and later it became a טרפה, or consecrated a fetus and it was born through the side. So we see that a fetus can become holy!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses רבי מאיר's explanation to show that consecrating a fetus works. That goes against בר פדא's opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר says the second half of the rule, 'do not make holy', is only needed for an animal that was already holy before it became flawed. One example he gives is a fetus that someone consecrated while it was still inside its mother, which was then born through the side. So consecrating a fetus in the womb must work, and that is hard for בר פדא.

keyTerms.meaning: It became a טרפה (got a fatal defect)
Fetus or newborn animal
Evidently; we see from here

steps.confusionAlert: רבי מאיר is not saying flawed animals can be consecrated after the flaw. He means they were holy first and became flawed later.

phrases.english: And it is taught: Rabbi Meir said:
Since they are not holy,
how could they make another animal holy?
You find this only
where one consecrates an animal and afterward it became a tereifa,
or where one consecrates a fetus and it came out through the side.
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets, 'through', is added in the corrected wording.

phrases.english: Evidently a fetus can become holy!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the ברייתא from step 10 and draws a conclusion that challenges בר פדא.
steps.kashyaTarget: בר פדא's opinion that a fetus cannot be consecrated
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי מאיר's case of a consecrated fetus born through the side only makes sense if consecrating a fetus in the womb works.

steps.title: בר פדא argues only when the mother is blemished
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that בר פדא agrees a healthy fetus inside a healthy mother can be consecrated. He argues with רבי יוחנן only about a healthy fetus inside a blemished mother.
steps.simpleTranslation: They answer: if an unblemished fetus is inside an unblemished mother, even בר פדא agrees it becomes holy. They argue only about an unblemished fetus inside a blemished mother. בר פדא holds: since the mother can't get קדושת הגוף, the fetus can't either. רבי יוחנן holds: they are like two separate animals. Only the mother can't become holy, but the fetus is holy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends בר פדא by narrowing what he and רבי יוחנן argue about. רבי מאיר's case can be about a healthy mother, where everyone agrees.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof from רבי מאיר only works if his fetus was inside a blemished mother, and it doesn't have to be. Their real argument is whether the fetus follows its mother. בר פדא says it does, so a blemished mother keeps the fetus from getting bodily holiness. רבי יוחנן says the fetus is its own animal.

keyTerms.meaning: An unblemished animal
A female animal with a blemish
Holiness of the body itself: the animal itself is holy and fit to be an offering
Like two separate animals

steps.whatToRemember: Everyone agrees that a healthy fetus in a healthy mother can be consecrated. בר פדא and רבי יוחנן argue only when the mother is blemished: does the fetus follow its mother, or is it a separate animal?

phrases.english: They say:
With an unblemished one in the womb of an unblemished mother,

phrases.english: even bar Padda agrees that it becomes holy.

about an unblemished one in the womb of a blemished mother.

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן דְּאִימֵּיהּ לָא מִקַּדְּשָׁא קְדוּשַּׁת הַגּוּף,

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי: בְּתָם בִּמְעֵי תְמִימָה, אֲפִילּוּ בַּר פְּדָא נָמֵי מוֹדֵי דְּקָדֵישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 11 by limiting where בר פדא disagrees.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the argument to a specific case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: בר פדא holds that a fetus can never be consecrated, so רבי מאיר's case goes against him.
steps.terutzMaskana: בר פדא disagrees only when the mother is blemished. רבי מאיר's case can be about a healthy mother, where everyone agrees.

steps.title: Another version: some flawed animals are found only as offspring of consecrated animals
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes another version of רבי מאיר's words. It says that holy כלאים, טומטום and אנדרוגינוס are found only as the offspring of consecrated animals.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another version: but a mixed-breed animal, a טומטום and an אנדרוגינוס, you find being holy only as the offspring of consecrated animals.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different version of how רבי מאיר's statement goes on. It covers the three flawed animals not explained in the first version.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first version explained only טרפה and יוצא דופן. Here רבי מאיר adds the other three. A holy animal of these kinds exists only when it gets its holiness as the offspring of a consecrated mother.

keyTerms.meaning: Another version of the discussion
Offspring of consecrated animals

phrases.english: Another version:
But a mixed-breed animal, a tumtum, and an androginos,

phrases.aramaic: אִי אַתָּה מוֹצֵא אֶלָּא בְּוַלְדֵי קֳדָשִׁים.
phrases.english: you find being holy only as offspring of consecrated animals.

steps.triggerLanguage: לִישָּׁנָא אַחֲרִינָא, אֲבָל כִּלְאַיִם וְטוּמְטוּם וְאַנְדְּרוֹגִינוֹס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a different version of how רבי מאיר's statement from step 11 continues.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A holy כלאים, טומטום or אנדרוגינוס is found only as the offspring of consecrated animals.

steps.title: Other fetuses can become holy, which challenges בר פדא
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר's second version ends by saying that רבי אליעזר holds like רבי יהודה, that offspring make תמורה. The גמרא infers that only these flawed offspring lack holiness of the body, but other fetuses do become holy. This goes against בר פדא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אליעזר holds like רבי יהודה, who used to say that the offspring of a holy animal can make a substitute. So it is only these flawed ones whose bodies cannot become holy. But other fetuses can become holy!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting רבי מאיר's second version. Then it draws an inference from it that seems to contradict בר פדא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version, the flawed offspring רבי מאיר is talking about are כלאים, טומטום and אנדרוגינוס, and they cannot become holy in their own body. That implies that normal offspring, and normal fetuses, can become holy in their own body. בר פדא held that a fetus cannot get that kind of holiness, so this looks like a challenge to him.

keyTerms.meaning: Offspring, the baby animal born to a holy animal
Makes a substitute: if someone swaps a regular animal for it, that animal becomes holy too
Their bodies become holy. This means real holiness of the animal itself, not just of its money value
Fetuses, unborn animals still inside the mother

steps.confusionAlert: The exclamation mark at the end is not a statement of the law. It is the גמרא raising a challenge against בר פדא, and the next step answers it.

phrases.english: And like Rabbi Yehuda, who would say:
phrases.notes: This is still רבי מאיר speaking. He means that רבי אליעזר holds like רבי יהודה.

phrases.english: The offspring makes a substitute.
It is only these whose bodies do not become holy,
phrases.notes: "These" are the three kinds just named in Step 13: כלאים, טומטום and אנדרוגינוס.

phrases.english: but other fetuses are holy!

steps.triggerLanguage: הָלֵין הוּא דְּלָא קָדְשִׁי גּוּפַיְיהוּ, אֲבָל עוּבָּרִין אֲחֵרִים קְדוֹשִׁין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: It finishes the second version of רבי מאיר's words from Step 13 and draws an inference from it against בר פדא.
steps.kashyaTarget: בר פדא's view that a fetus cannot become holy in its own body
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Only these flawed offspring (כלאים, טומטום, אנדרוגינוס) are excluded from holiness of the body. That implies normal fetuses do get holiness of the body, which goes against בר פדא.

steps.title: אביי: the argument is only about a fetus inside a blemished mother
steps.stepSummary: אביי says everyone agrees that a healthy fetus inside a healthy mother becomes holy in its own body. בר פדא and רבי יוחנן argue only about a healthy fetus inside a blemished mother. בר פדא follows the mother, and רבי יוחנן treats the fetus as separate.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: a healthy fetus inside a healthy mother becomes holy in its own body, and everyone agrees to that. They argue only when it is inside a blemished mother. בר פדא holds that since the mother's body cannot become holy, the fetus also becomes holy only for its value. רבי יוחנן holds that a fetus is not just a part of its mother. So even though the mother's body is not holy, the offspring's body is holy.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the challenge. He narrows the argument between בר פדא and רבי יוחנן so that בר פדא does not contradict the inference from רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The inference only shows that a fetus can become holy in a normal case, a healthy fetus in a healthy mother, and בר פדא agrees to that. Their real argument is whether a fetus follows its mother. בר פדא says the fetus follows a blemished mother and gets holiness of value only. רבי יוחנן says the fetus is its own animal, so it can become holy in its body.

keyTerms.meaning: Healthy, without a blemish (said of the fetus)
A healthy, unblemished mother animal
A mother animal with a blemish that makes it unfit for the מזבח
For its value: only its money worth is holy, not the animal's body itself
A fetus is like the thigh of its mother, meaning it is treated as a part of her body

steps.whatToRemember: Healthy fetus in a healthy mother: everyone agrees its body is holy. Healthy fetus in a blemished mother: בר פדא says it is holy only for its value because it follows its mother. רבי יוחנן says its body is holy because a fetus is not part of its mother.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the exact boundary of the argument between בר פדא and רבי יוחנן. It hangs on the well-known question of whether a fetus counts as part of its mother.

phrases.english: Abaye said: an unblemished one in the womb of an unblemished mother —
everyone agrees its body becomes holy,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא כִּי פְּלִיגִי בִּמְעֵי בַּעֲלַת מוּם,
phrases.english: rather, where they argue is in the womb of a blemished mother,
phrases.notes: "They" means בר פדא and רבי יוחנן, and the fetus itself is still healthy.

phrases.english: for bar Padda holds:

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן דְּאִימֵּיהּ נָמֵי לָא קָדֵישׁ גּוּפַהּ —
phrases.english: since its mother's body also does not become holy —

phrases.aramaic: אִיהוּ נָמֵי לָא קָדֵישׁ אֶלָּא לִדְמֵי,
phrases.english: it too becomes holy only for its value,
Rabbi Yochanan holds:
a fetus is not the thigh of its mother,
phrases.notes: He means the fetus is not just a part of the mother's body. It is its own animal.

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף עַל גַּב דְּאִימֵּיהּ לָא קָדְשָׁה לְגוּפַהּ —
phrases.english: and even though its mother is not holy in her body —
the offspring at least is holy in its body.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: תָּם בִּמְעֵי תְּמִימָה דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל קָדֵישׁ גּוּפֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: It answers the challenge from Step 14 by limiting the argument to a fetus inside a blemished mother.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the argument to a specific case (אוקימתא of the argument)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought בר פדא holds that no fetus can ever become holy in its body, so the inference from רבי מאיר would contradict him.
steps.terutzMaskana: בר פדא agrees that a healthy fetus in a healthy mother becomes holy in its body. He disagrees only when the mother is blemished, because he holds that the fetus follows its mother.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: consecrating the leg of an animal makes the whole animal holy
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns to a new line of the משנה. רבי יוסי argues that just as saying 'the leg of this one is an עולה' makes the whole animal holy, swapping using limbs should also work for תמורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי said: With holy animals, isn't it true that someone who says 'the leg of this one is an עולה' makes the whole animal an עולה? (So the same should be true for תמורה.)
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting the next part of the משנה. This is a setup line, and the discussion of רבי יוסי's view follows after it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, the חכמים say you cannot make a תמורה by swapping limbs of a regular animal for whole holy animals. רבי יוסי disagrees. He points out that when someone consecrates just one limb of an animal, the holiness spreads to the whole animal, and he wants the same rule for תמורה.

keyTerms.meaning: Consecrated animals, set aside as קרבנות
'The leg of this one', when someone consecrates only one limb of an animal
And so on: the rest of the משנה's words are not written out here

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei said: But isn't it so with consecrated animals,
that one who says 'the leg of this one' etc.
phrases.notes: The "etc." stands for the rest of the משנה: 'is an עולה', and then the whole animal becomes an עולה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי: וַהֲלֹא בְּמוּקְדָּשִׁין, הָאוֹמֵר רַגְלָהּ שֶׁל זוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: It leaves the discussion about fetuses and opens a new section on רבי יוסי's view in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוסי holds that consecrating one limb of an animal makes the whole animal holy, and he uses this to argue that limbs can also make a תמורה.
